delivered: The main workspace accepts complete native EventTable JSON as an active source, with literal case/activity/timestamp/resource/lifecycle selectors and explicit log, stream, dataframe or lazyframe dispatch. Original CSV/XES inputs remain available and preserve their actual native import and grouped-log defaults.

An immutable owned source retains the original uploaded bytes, full typed original and checked tables, actual prepared log/stream/lazy views, raw native stored state and explicit preparation failures. Physical row ordinals, representative native grouping provenance and projection changes are separate from original values, dtypes, categories, index labels and table metadata.

Independent mining and analysis consumers report their actual native input kind, complete options, execution status, full native result and native error. Successful flat consumers and original input remain available when grouped-log preparation or classic analysis fails; unavailable logs/models are guarded explicitly rather than inferred from empty results.

Cached analysis, filtering, queries, clustering and model evaluation use the owned source or an explicitly required native grouped-log/model view. Source-only inputs provide inspection and event SQL/JSON export with nullable case counts. Query selection uses positional provenance and does not merge duplicate trace identities or rewrite original typed cells.

Default CSV alias bindings follow the physical headers selected by the native importer. Exact columns and explicit literal selectors keep precedence; empty/header-only inputs use the same native aliases and conditional case fallback. Physical flat bindings do not alter legacy grouped-log ordering defaults. A paired CSV schema failure may preserve an actual accepted legacy LOG with its derived-table origin and explicit paired-import error.

The unchanged original typed file and source settings can be reused in seven independent workflows: Alpha/Heuristic, Inductive, graph/decomposed alignment, process-tree alignment, anti/multi alignment, token replay and Petri alignment. Their original models and native prepared inputs remain separate from the active source.

UUID request generation, cancellation and accepted-source identity prevent replaced or canceled mining requests and late client completions from publishing stale state. A late cancellation cannot roll back a newer source or an explicitly edited model clone. Frontend caches are invalidated and rebound to the accepted source.

Complete original/request/report/raw-result/artifact downloads, every inspection CSV and selected native record preserve exact integer tokens, negative zero and UTF/WTF-8 text. SQL uses exact byte request bodies. Captured fixtures retain every original request/response/upload/export byte with independent integrity checks and casefold collision protection.
boundaries: This checkpoint is feature delivery with own-source native, API, export and frontend evidence. It does not establish full PM4Py behavioral parity or promote any catalogue unit. All 86 packages, 387 modules and 228 incomplete strict units remain in scope.

The exact-origin browser retry after the user enabled settings was rejected by the browser tool as a saved permission or managed policy denial. It occurred while Feature56 was served on port8562 and loaded no UI. The coherent Feature57 HTTP/API/production-asset checks are separate evidence; browser interactions, downloads, screenshots and responsive checks remain pending.

Native log-only consumers require successful grouped-log preparation. RelatedLogs and Streaming current-source reuse remain guarded for typed inputs. The cached concept-drift route still invokes the EventLog BOSE overload; the native EventTable BOSE overload is not claimed as delivered here.

Projection row lineage identifies actual native representative rows; it is not a complete ancestry claim for synthetic or grouped events. SQLite projections may expose large unsigned integers as text without modifying the source. CSV native string dtypes are retained and may legitimately cause mutable pandas native datetime errors.

Every failed API fixture expectation remains preserved and excluded from completed validation counts. Earlier successful native/frontend builds are superseded where a genuine source or request-byte correction required a fresh immutable build; executed recipes and old results are not rewritten.

The first export validation identified a frontend upload-recognition defect: a canonical response guard rejected native-valid original tables with empty metadata defaults. A separate structural input candidate guard now accepts those original uploads and preserves their raw bytes while the native parser validates semantics; canonical response validation is unchanged. The failed proof and its exact frontend source snapshot remain retained and excluded from completed counts.

Exact reference defaults, ordering, types, error contracts, Unicode, solver behavior, marking semantics, concurrency and performance remain independent gates. Original-model Monte Carlo, Petri/DFG/process-tree playout and independent normative decision inputs remain feature-first work beyond this checkpoint.
